1. Heard learned counsel for the applicants and Shri Sandeep Kumar Kushwaha,, learned counsel for
the opposite party no. 2 as well as learned Aga for the state.

2.  This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed with the prayer to quash the entire proceedings of Case no. 567 of 2017 (State vs. Mohit Arora and Others), arising out of Case Crime No.0567 of 2017, under Sections 420, 406 IPC, P.S. Bisrakh, District- Gautam Budh Nagar, pending in the court of District and Sessions Judge, Gautam Budh Nagar.

3. Pursuant to order dated 11.02.2022, the parties appeared before the court below for verification of settlement / compromise, who were duly identified by their counsel's, while verifying the compromise / settlement dated 11.04.2023.
4.

It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that all the disputes and differences have been Mr. Mohit Arora And 2 Others vs State Of U.P And 3 Others on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172943221/
1 settled between the parties.

sentences.text: At this stage, learned counsel further submitted that continuation of the proceedings of the aforesaid case will be an abuse of process of law.
No fruitful purpose would be served by keeping the matter pending.

In support of his contention, learned counsel for the applicant has also placed reliance on the law laid down by Apex Court in Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab, (2012), 10 SCC 303, B.S. Joshi and others vs. State of Haryana and another, (2003) 4 SCC 675 and Madan Mohan Abbot vs. State of Punjab, (2008) 4 SCC 582.
5.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 submits that since the dispute between the parties has been settled, opposite party no.2 has no objection if the proceedings of the aforesaid complaint case pending before the trial court is quashed.
6. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the entire record.

7. In all the aforesaid cases, the Apex Court has laid down the law that criminal proceedings may be quashed even in non-compoundable cases by the High Court in exercise of its extraordinary jurisdiction to restore peace between the parties and in case the justice so demands.

According to Hon'ble Supreme Court, if the offence involve private dispute between the parties of commercial nature or matrimonial dispute and it is not related to heinous offence, the proceedings may be quashed.
8. The facts and circumstances as stated hereinabove are peculiar in the present case.

From perusal of the record, it is apparent that in pursuance of settlement agreement, which has been signed between the parties, the respondent no.4 has taken physical possession of the flat bearing no.B15/1805, Eco Village-2 project and to this effect a handing/ taking over the flat was also exuted on 22 September.

It also appears that once the physical possession of the flat has been taken by the respondent no.4/ informant after setting his all issues/ grievances fully an finally, with the company and no claim/ grievances/ disputes of any nature survives in between the parties now.

As such,
looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, no mental depravity is involved in the case.
If the request of the parties is denied, it will be amounting to only adding one more criminal case to the already overburdened criminal courts.

9. Since the dispute between the parties has been amicably and mutually settled, no fruitful purpose would be served by permitting to continue the criminal case pending before the trial court and it would simply be a waste of time if the aforesaid case is permitted to continue till its logical conclusion.
10. In view of the above, the Application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. is allowed.

11. The entire proceedings of Case no. 567 of 2017 (State vs. Mohit Arora and Others), arising out of Case Crime No.0567 of 2017, under Sections 420, 406 IPC, P.S. Bisrakh, District- Gautam Budh Nagar, pending in the court of District and Sessions Judge, Gautam Budh Nagar, against the applicant are quashed in terms of compromise arrived at between the parties.
